'''Steven Elliot Koonin''' (born December 12, 1951)<ref>{{cite web|title=Steven Koonin|url=http://www.aip.org/history/acap/biographies/bio.jsp?koonins|website=Array of Contemporary American Physicists|publisher=[[American Institute of Physics]]|access-date=20 September 2014|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150331135114/http://www.aip.org/history/acap/biographies/bio.jsp?koonins|archive-date=31 March 2015}}</ref> is an American [[theoretical physicist]], [[Environmental science|environmental scientist]], and former director of the [[Center for Urban Science and Progress]] at [[New York University]]. He is also a professor in the Department of Civil and Urban Engineering at NYU's [[New York University Tandon School of Engineering|Tandon School of Engineering]].<ref>{{Cite web | url=https://engineering.nyu.edu/people/steven-e-koonin |title = Steven Koonin|publisher=NYU Tandon School of Engineering}}</ref> From 2004 to 2009, Koonin was employed by [[BP]] as the oil and gas company’s Chief Scientist.<ref>{{cite web|title=Steven E. Koonin – Director – NYU's Center for Urban Science & Progress and Former Under Secretary for Science|url=https://www.energy.gov/seab/contributors/steven-e-koonin|access-date=11 May 2021|website=energy.gov|publisher=US DOE}}</ref> From 2009 to 2011, he was [[Under Secretary of Energy for Science and Innovation|Under Secretary for Science]], Department of Energy, in the [[Obama administration]]. He later published ''Unsettled: What Climate Science Tells Us, What It Doesn't, and Why It Matters,'' for which he was widely condemned for promoting [[Climate change denial|climate denial]] and labeled a climate change skeptic.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Clement |first=Naomi Oreskes, Michael E. Mann, Gernot Wagner, Don Wuebbles, Andrew Dessler, Andrea Dutton, Geoffrey Supran, Matthew Huber, Thomas Lovejoy, Ilissa Ocko, Peter C. Frumhoff, Joel |title=That 'Obama Scientist' Climate Skeptic You've Been Hearing About ... |url=https://www.scientificamerican.com/article/that-obama-scientist-climate-skeptic-youve-been-hearing-about/ |access-date=2025-06-29 |website=Scientific American |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=MacDonald |first=Ted |date=2021-05-11 |title=Right-wing media are having a field day with physicist Steve Koonin's new book of climate misinformation |url=https://www.mediamatters.org/climate-deniers/right-wing-media-are-having-field-day-physicist-steve-koonins-new-book-climate |access-date=2025-06-29 |website=Media Matters for America |language=en}}</ref><ref name=ClimateFeedback>{{Cite web |date=May 3, 2021 |title=Wall Street Journal article repeats multiple incorrect and misleading claims made in Steven Koonin's new book 'Unsettled' |first=Boris |last=Bellanger |url=https://science.feedback.org/review/wall-street-journal-article-repeats-multiple-incorrect-and-misleading-claims-made-in-steven-koonins-new-book-unsettled-steven-koonin/ |access-date=March 14, 2026 |website=[[Climate Feedback]] |publisher=Science Feedback |language=en-US}}</ref> In 2024, he became the Edward Teller Fellow at [[Stanford University]]'s [[Hoover Institution]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Steven Koonin |url=https://www.hoover.org/profiles/steven-koonin |access-date=2025-05-14 |website=Hoover Institution |language=en}}</ref> In 2025, he was member of the United States Department of Energy's Climate Working Group -formed by five researchers who reject the scientific consensus on climate change- and coauthor the [[United States Department of Energy|U.S. Department of Energy]] draft report, ''[[A Critical Review of Impacts of Greenhouse Gas Emissions on the U.S. Climate]]'' that asserted that the danger from greenhouse gas emissions was exaggerated.<ref name=report/><ref>{{Cite web |last=Storrow |first=Benjamin |date=2025-08-11 |title=How Chris Wright recruited a team to upend climate science |url=https://www.eenews.net/articles/how-chris-wright-recruited-a-team-to-upend-climate-science-2/ |access-date=2025-09-22 |website=E&E News by POLITICO |language=en-US}}</ref>

==Biography==
Born in [[Brooklyn]], New York City, Koonin graduated from [[Stuyvesant High School]] at the age of 16, received his [[Bachelor of Science]] from the [[California Institute of Technology]] and his [[Ph.D.]] from the [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]] under the supervision of [[Arthur Kerman]] in the [[MIT Center for Theoretical Physics]].<ref>{{Cite web | url=https://web.mit.edu/newsoffice/2010/hottel-koonin-0923.html |title = Frank talk on U.S. Energy innovation| date=23 September 2010 }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://history.aip.org/phn/11603032.html|title=Koonin, Steven E.|website=history.aip.org|access-date=2019-12-30}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://news.mit.edu/2017/professor-emeritus-arthur-kerman-of-physics-dies-0602|title=Arthur Kerman, professor emeritus of physics, dies at 88|website=MIT News|date=2 June 2017 |access-date=2019-12-30}}</ref> In 1975, Koonin joined the faculty of the California Institute of Technology as an assistant professor of [[theoretical physics]] becoming one of their youngest ever faculty, and served as the institute's [[Provost (education)|provost]] from 1995 to 2004.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.caltech.edu/content/former-caltech-provost-steven-koonin-nominated-under-secretary-science |title=Former Caltech Provost Steven Koonin Nominated for Under Secretary for Science {{!}} Caltech |website=www.caltech.edu |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141207174156/http://www.caltech.edu/content/former-caltech-provost-steven-koonin-nominated-under-secretary-science |archive-date=2014-12-07}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.caltech.edu/news/caltech-appoints-physicist-steve-koonin-new-provost-11|title=Caltech Appoints Physicist Steve Koonin New Provost|publisher=California Institute of Technology|access-date=2018-12-20}}</ref> During his tenure as provost, he was involved in projects related to [[Computational science|scientific computing]], [[Biological engineering|bioengineering]], and [[biology]].<ref name=":1">{{Cite web |title=Steven E. Koonin |url=https://www.energy.gov/seab/person/steven-e-koonin#:~:text=at%20Urbana-Champaign.-,Dr.,with%20the%20Monte%20Carlo%20technique.%E2%80%9D |access-date=2025-05-14 |website=Energy.gov |language=en}}</ref><ref name=":2">{{Cite web |date=2025-04-19 |title=Steven Koonin |url=https://www.ceraweek.com/en/speakers/steven-koonin-1060-24629 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250419025055/https://www.ceraweek.com/en/speakers/steven-koonin-1060-24629 |archive-date=April 19, 2025 |access-date=2025-05-14 }}</ref>  He oversaw institutional support for large-scale research projects, including the development of the [[Thirty Meter Telescope|Thirty-Meter Telescope]] project.<ref>{{cite web |last=Case |first=Fiona |date=2007-10-01 |title='I had always wondered what the private sector was like' |url=https://www.chemistryworld.com/careers/i-had-always-wondered-what-the-private-sector-was-like/3006807.article |access-date=2025-05-14 |website=Chemistry World }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2001-12-02 |title=Super Telescope Could Get Lift From Large Caltech Donation |url=https://www.ocbj.com/news/super-telescope-could-get-lift-from-large-caltech/ |access-date=2025-05-14 |website=Orange County Business Journal |language=en-US}}</ref><ref name=":1" />

In 2004, Koonin joined [[BP]] as their chief scientist, where he was responsible for guiding the company's long-range technology strategy, particularly in alternative and [[renewable energy]] sources.<ref>{{cite web |title=Steven E. Koonin – Director – NYU's Center for Urban Science & Progress and Former Under Secretary for Science |url=https://www.energy.gov/seab/contributors/steven-e-koonin |website=energy.gov |publisher=US DOE |access-date=11 May 2021}}</ref> He was tapped for the position of [[Under Secretary for Science]] at the [[United States Department of Energy]] by [[Steven Chu]], Obama's Secretary of Energy,<ref name="misleading"/> and served from May 19, 2009, to November 18, 2011.<ref>[https://obamawhitehouse.archives.gov/the_press_office/President-Obama-Announces-More-Key-Administration-Posts-3-20-09/ President Obama Announces More Key Administration Posts]</ref><ref>[http://energy.gov/contributors/steven-e-koonin Energy.gov: "Dr. Steven E. Koonin – Director – NYU's Center for Urban Science & Progress and Former Under Secretary for Science"] retrieved October 20, 2013</ref> At the Department of Energy, Koonin was involved in the climate research program and energy technology policy. He was the lead author of the agency's 2011 Strategic Plan and the first Quadrennial Technology review.<ref name="Communications">{{Cite web |last=Communications |first=NYU Web |title=NYU Names Renowned Physicist Steven Koonin Director of New Center for Urban Science and Progress |url=https://www.nyu.edu/about/news-publications/news/2012/april/nyu-names-renowned-physicist-steven-koonin-director-of-new-center-for-urban-science-and-progress.html |access-date=2025-05-14 |website=www.nyu.edu |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2011-11-15 |title=Quadrennial Energy and Technology Reviews |url=https://energy.mit.edu/news/quadrennial-energy-and-technology-reviews/ |access-date=2025-05-14 |website=Main |language=en}}</ref> Koonin left in November 2011 for a position at the [[Institute for Defense Analyses]].<ref>{{Cite journal |date=2011-11-18 |title=Newsmakers |url=https://www.science.org/doi/10.1126/science.334.6058.881-b#:~:text=Steven%20Koonin%20is%20leaving%20his%20job%20as%20undersecretary&text=Koonin's%20next%20stop%20is%20the%20Institute%20for%20Defense%20Analyses'%20Science%20and%20Technology%20Policy%20Institute |journal=Science |volume=334 |issue=6058 |pages=881–882 |doi=10.1126/science.334.6058.881-b|url-access=subscription }}</ref> In 2012, he was appointed the founding director of [[New York University|NYU]]'s [[Center for Urban Science and Progress]] (CUSP),<ref>{{Cite web | url=https://cusp.nyu.edu/profiles/steve-koonin/ |title = Steve Koonin |access-date=August 15, 2021}}</ref> an applied research center which uses data to study [[Urban informatics|urban challenges]].<ref name="Communications"/>

At NYU, Koonin was appointed to the [[New York University Stern School of Business|Stern School of Business]], the [[New York University Tandon School of Engineering|Tandon School of Engineering]], and the Department of Physics.<ref name=":2" /> He has served on numerous advisory bodies for the [[National Science Foundation]], the [[United States Department of Defense|Department of Defense]], and the [[United States Department of Energy|Department of Energy]] and its various national laboratories, such as the [[JASON (advisory group)|JASON defense advisory group]], which he has chaired.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://energy.gov/contributors/steven-e-koonin|title=Steven Koonin|publisher=Department of Energy}}</ref> From 2014 to 2019, he chaired the National Academies' Diversional Committee for Engineering and Physical Sciences.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Unsettling Climate Science {{!}} Claremont McKenna College |url=https://www.cmc.edu/athenaeum/unsettling-climate-science |access-date=2025-05-14 |website=www.cmc.edu |language=en}}</ref> From 2014 to 2024, he was a trustee of the [[Institute for Defense Analyses]].<ref name=":2" /> Koonin's research interests have included theoretical nuclear, [[Many-body theory|many-body]], and [[computational physics]], [[nuclear astrophysics]], and global [[environmental science]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.pma.caltech.edu/PhysColl/biographies/people/koonin_steven.html |title=Physics Research Conference – Speaker: Dr. Steven E. Koonin|publisher=[[California Institute of Technology]], The Division of Physics, Mathematics and Astronomy|access-date=2014-07-18 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100623190822/http://www.pma.caltech.edu/PhysColl/biographies/people/koonin_steven.html |archive-date=2010-06-23 }}</ref> He is a fellow of the [[American Academy of Arts and Sciences]]<ref>{{Cite web |date=2009-03-25 |title=Former Caltech Provost Steven Koonin Nominated for Under Secretary for Science |url=https://www.caltech.edu/about/news/former-caltech-provost-steven-koonin-nominated-under-secretary-science-1521 |access-date=2025-05-14 |website=California Institute of Technology |language=en}}</ref> and a member of the [[National Academy of Sciences]].<ref name=":2" />

He was awarded the prestigious Barry Prize for Distinguished Intellectual Achievement by the American Academy of Sciences and Letters in 2023.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Awards |url=https://academysciencesletters.org/awards/ |access-date=2024-10-27 |website=American Academy of Sciences & Letters |language=en-US}}</ref>

== Cold fusion ==
Koonin played a major role in the 1989 national controversy around [[cold fusion]] sparked by the research of [[Martin Fleischmann]] and [[Stanley Pons]]. After the explosive announcement of their research at the [[University of Utah]], excitement for the potential of fusion as an energy source quickly gave way to skepticism among the scientific community as scientists across the world raced to replicate the Utah experiment.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Ritter |first1=Stanley K. |title=Cold fusion died 25 years ago, but the research lives on |url=https://cen.acs.org/articles/94/i44/Cold-fusion-died-25-years.html |website=Chemical & Engineering News |language=en}}</ref> Steven Koonin and his [[Caltech]] colleagues, [[Nathan Lewis (chemist)|Nathan Lewis]] and Charles Barnes (who became known as the "Caltech Three") headed up a research group to investigate cold fusion.<ref name="cold fusion 3" />

The scientific skepticism around cold fusion came to a head at the meeting of the [[American Physical Society]] in [[Baltimore]] later in 1989.<ref name="NYT">{{cite web |last1=Browne |first1=Malcom W. |title=Physicists Debunk Claim Of a New Kind of Fusion |url=https://www.nytimes.com/1989/05/03/us/physicists-debunk-claim-of-a-new-kind-of-fusion.html |work=New York Times |access-date=1 November 2024}}</ref> At the conference, Steven Koonin,  and Nathan Lewis gave devastating presentations based on the work of the Caltech cold fusion research group.<ref name="cold fusion 3">{{cite web |last1=Goodstein |first1=David L. |title=Whatever Happened to Cold Fusion? |url=https://calteches.library.caltech.edu/3782/1/Goodstein.pdf |website=Caltech |access-date=1 November 2024}}</ref> During his presentation, Koonin called the Utah publication of the Utah research a result of "the incompetence and delusion of Pons and Fleischmann," which was met with a standing ovation.<ref>{{Cite book| last=Taubes | first=Gary| author-link=Gary Taubes| title=Bad Science: The Short Life and Weird Times of Cold Fusion| location=New York| publisher=Random House| year=1993|page=266 |isbn=978-0-394-58456-0|title-link=Bad Science: The Short Life and Weird Times of Cold Fusion }}</ref> Initially Koonin had intended to go further, potentially calling the Pons-Fleischmann research fraudulent, however he was counseled to avoid using the term "fraud" by peers and by Caltech president, [[Thomas Eugene Everhart|Thomas E. Everhart]].<ref name="CAB">{{cite web |last=Aspaturian |first=Heidi |date=14 December 2012<!-- pdf metadata, archive record page updated 2012-12-26 --> |title=Interview with Charles A. Barnes on 13 and 26 June 1989 |publisher=The Caltech Institute Archives |url=http://resolver.caltech.edu/CaltechOH:OH_Barnes_C_coldfusion |access-date=22 August 2014}}</ref> These presentations of the Caltech group revealed serious deficiencies in cold fusion research and ultimately led to mainstream science's rejection of cold fusion.<ref name="cold fusion 3" />

== Views on climate change ==
Koonin became publicly involved in the policy debate about climate change starting with a ''Wall Street Journal'' opinion piece in 2017, in which he floated the idea of a [[red team]]/blue team exercise for climate science. In 2018, the [[United States Environmental Protection Agency|Environmental Protection Agency]] (EPA) under the leadership of [[Scott Pruitt]] proposed a public debate on climate change to refute the 2017 [[Climate Science Special Report]]. According to a draft press release edited by Koonin and William Happer, Princeton physics professor and director of the [[CO2 Coalition|CO<sub>2</sub> Coalition]], they planned "red team"/blue team exercises to challenge the [[Scientific consensus on climate change|scientific consensus on climate]]. The draft was never released, and the plans were not carried out.<ref>{{cite news |last=Hirji |first=Zahra |url=https://www.buzzfeednews.com/article/zahrahirji/epa-climate-debate-press-release |title=Here's The EPA Press Release Announcing The "Red Team/Blue Team" Climate Debate That Never Happened |work=[[BuzzFeed News]] |date=May 15, 2018 |access-date=August 14, 2021}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|last1=Bravender|first1=Robin|date=June 13, 2018|title=Obama official would have led EPA's climate science debate—if all agencies took part|url=https://www.science.org/content/article/obama-official-would-have-led-epa-s-climate-science-debate-if-all-agencies-took-part|access-date=2020-12-20|website=[[Science (journal)|Science]]|publisher=[[American Association for the Advancement of Science]]}}</ref><ref name="skeptics">{{Cite web|first=Scott|last=Waldman|title=Skeptics Are Being Recruited for an "Adversarial" Review of Climate Science|url=https://www.scientificamerican.com/article/skeptics-are-being-recruited-for-an-adversarial-review-of-climate-science/|access-date=2020-12-20|work=[[Scientific American]]}}</ref>

In 2019, the [[First presidency of Donald Trump|Trump Administration]] proposed to create a "Presidential Committee on Climate Security" at the National Security Council that would conduct an "adversarial" review of the scientific consensus on climate change. Koonin was actively involved in recruiting others to be part of this review. The committee was scrapped in favor of an initiative not "subject to the same level of public disclosure as a formal advisory committee".<ref name="skeptics"/><ref>{{cite news |last1=Eilperin |first1=Juliet |last2=Ryan |first2=Missy |url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/national/health-science/white-house-readies-panel-to-assess-if-climate-change-poses-a-national-security-threat/2019/02/19/ccc8b29e-3396-11e9-af5b-b51b7ff322e9_story.html |title=White House prepares to scrutinize intelligence agencies' finding that climate change threatens national security |newspaper=[[The Washington Post]] |date=February 20, 2019 |access-date=August 14, 2021}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last1=Eilperin |first1=Juliet |last2=Dawsey |first2=Josh |last3=Dennis |first3=Brady |url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/national/health-science/white-house-to-select-federal-scientists-to-reassess-government-climate-findings-sources-say/2019/02/24/49cd0a84-37dd-11e9-af5b-b51b7ff322e9_story.html |title=White House to set up panel to counter climate change consensus, officials say |newspaper=[[The Washington Post]] |date=February 24, 2019 |access-date=August 14, 2021}}</ref>

Koonin is a coauthor of the July 23, 2025, [[United States Department of Energy|U.S. Department of Energy]] report, ''[[A Critical Review of Impacts of Greenhouse Gas Emissions on the U.S. Climate]]'' that asserted that the danger from greenhouse gas emissions was exaggerated.<ref name=report>{{cite web |last1=Rowley |first1=Madeleine|date=August 19, 2025 |title=Steven Koonin: The Truth About Climate Change 'Lies Somewhere in the Middle' |url=https://www.thefp.com/p/the-truth-about-climate-change-lies-middle-steve-koonin |website=thefp.com |publisher=[[The Free Press (Paramount Skydance)|The Free Press]] |access-date=23 October 2025}}</ref> In an interview with [[The Free Press (Paramount Skydance)|The Free Press]], Koonin claimed that "Ninety-five percent of the report is sourced from" the [[United Nations]] [[Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change]] (IPCC) report.<ref name=report/><ref>{{cite web |title=The Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change |url=https://www.ipcc.ch/ |website=ipcc.ch |publisher=[[United Nations]] |access-date=20 August 2025}}</ref> The report has been criticized for cherry-picking and for highlighting uncertainties in order to downplay the impacts of climate change. Furthermore, numerous scientists whose work was cited by the report indicated that their work had been mischaracterized.<ref name=":3">{{Cite web |title=Contrarian climate assessment from U.S. government draws swift pushback |url=https://www.science.org/content/article/contrarian-climate-assessment-u-s-government-draws-swift-pushback |access-date=2025-08-20 |website=www.science.org |language=en}}</ref>

===2014 ''Wall Street Journal'' commentary===
Koonin wrote a 2000-word essay, "Climate Science Is Not Settled," that was published in an issue of ''[[The Wall Street Journal]]''.<ref>{{cite news |last=Koonin |first=Steven E.|title=Climate Science Is Not Settled |url=https://www.wsj.com/articles/climate-science-is-not-settled-1411143565 |access-date=16 May 2021 |work=[[The Wall Street Journal]] |date=September 19, 2014 | url-access=subscription}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://friendsofscience.org/assets/documents/Climate%20Science%20Is%20Not%20Settled.pdf |title=Climate Science is Not Settled |access-date=2024-02-28}}</ref> The main points of the article were that:
* the limits of climate measurement data make it hard to untangle the planet's response to human influences, from natural changes that are poorly understood.
* The results of various climate models disagree with or contradict each other.
* Press releases, summaries, headlines, and news stories often don't accurately reflect the consensus among scientists.
* The science is not mature enough to make useful projections about the future of the climate, nor what effects past or future human actions might have on it.

In an article in [[Slate (magazine)|''Slate'']],<ref>{{cite web |last1=Pierrehumbert |first1=Raymond |author1-link=Raymond Pierrehumbert |title=Climate Science Is Settled ''Enough'' |url=https://slate.com/technology/2014/10/the-wall-street-journal-and-steve-koonin-the-new-face-of-climate-change-inaction.html |work=[[Slate (magazine)|Slate]] |date=October 1, 2014 |access-date=May 16, 2021}}</ref> climate physicist [[Raymond Pierrehumbert]] criticized Koonin's essay as "a litany of discredited arguments" with "nuggets of truth ... buried beneath a rubble of false or misleading claims from the standard climate skeptics' canon."

===2021 book ''Unsettled''===
{{anchor|Unsettled|unsettled}}
In 2021, Koonin published the book ''Unsettled: What Climate Science Tells Us, What It Doesn't, and Why It Matters''.<ref name=Yohe/> Critics accused him of [[cherry picking]] data, muddying the waters surrounding the [[Scientific consensus on climate change|science of climate change]], and having no experience in [[Climatology|climate science]], all points he rebukes in the opening of his book.<ref name=":0">{{Cite news|author=''National Post'' staff|date=2 September 2021|title=The unalarmist: Steven Koonin's controversial climate contentions|work=[[National Post]]|url=https://nationalpost.com/news/world/the-unalarmist-steven-koonins-controversial-climate-contentions|access-date=2021-10-25}}</ref>

In a review in ''[[Scientific American]]'', economist [[Gary Yohe]] wrote that Koonin "falsely suggest[s] that we don't understand the risks well enough to take action":{{blockquote|The science is stronger than ever around findings that speak to the likelihood and consequences of climate impacts, and has been growing stronger for decades. In the early days of research, the uncertainty was wide; but with each subsequent step that uncertainty has narrowed or become better understood. This is how science works, and in the case of climate, the early indications detected and attributed in the 1980s and 1990s, have come true, over and over again and sooner than anticipated...

[Decision makers] are using the best and most honest science to inform prospective investments in abatement (reducing greenhouse gas emissions to diminish the estimated likelihoods of dangerous climate change impacts) and adaptation (reducing vulnerabilities to diminish their current and projected consequences).<ref name=Yohe>{{cite web |last=Yohe |first=Gary |author-link=Gary Yohe |title=A New Book Manages to Get Climate Science Badly Wrong|date=May 13, 2021|url=https://www.scientificamerican.com/article/a-new-book-manages-to-get-climate-science-badly-wrong/ |website=[[Scientific American]] |access-date=16 May 2021}}</ref>}}

Physicist [[Mark Boslough]], a former student of Koonin, posted a critical review at [[Yale Climate Connections]]. He stated that "Koonin makes use of an old strawman concocted by opponents of climate science in the 1990s to create an illusion of arrogant scientists, biased media, and lying politicians – making them easier to attack."<ref>{{cite web |last=Boslough |first=Mark |author1-link=Mark Boslough |title=A critical review of Steven Koonin's 'Unsettled' |url=https://yaleclimateconnections.org/2021/05/a-critical-review-of-steven-koonins-unsettled/ |website=[[Yale Climate Connections]] |publisher=The Yale Center for Environmental Communication |date=May 25, 2021|access-date=August 14, 2021}}</ref>

Nonprofit organization ''[[Inside Climate News]]'' reported that climate scientists call Koonin's conclusions "fatally out of date ... and based on the 2013 physical science report of the [[Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change]] (IPCC)."<ref name="misleading">{{cite news |last=Lavelle |first=Marianne |url=https://insideclimatenews.org/news/04052021/a-new-book-feeds-climate-doubters-but-scientists-say-the-conclusions-are-misleading-and-out-of-date/ |title=A New Book Feeds Climate Doubters, but Scientists Say the Conclusions are Misleading and Out of Date |work=[[Inside Climate News]] |date=May 4, 2021 |access-date=August 14, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210505124154/https://insideclimatenews.org/news/04052021/a-new-book-feeds-climate-doubters-but-scientists-say-the-conclusions-are-misleading-and-out-of-date/ |archive-date=May 5, 2021}}</ref>

Mark P. Mills, a senior fellow at the [[Manhattan Institute for Policy Research|Manhattan Institute]], a conservative think tank, and faculty fellow at [[Northwestern University]]’s McCormick School of Engineering and Applied Science,<ref>{{Cite web |title=Mark P. Mills |url=https://www.manhattan-institute.org/expert/mark-p-mills |access-date=2022-07-23 |website=Manhattan Institute |language=en}}</ref> lauded the book in ''[[The Wall Street Journal]]'' as "rebut[ing] much of the dominant political narrative".<ref>{{Cite news |last=Mills |first=Mark P. |date=2021-04-25 |title='Unsettled' Review: The 'Consensus' On Climate |language=en-US |work=The Wall Street Journal |url=https://www.wsj.com/articles/unsettled-review-theconsensus-on-climate-11619383653 |access-date= |issn=0099-9660}}</ref> Twelve scientists analyzed Mills's arguments and said that he merely repeated Koonin's incorrect and misleading claims.<ref name=ClimateFeedback /> Koonin responded with a post on [[Medium (website)|Medium]] answering these critics.<ref>{{Cite web |title= A bad check of climate facts |url=https://steven-koonin.medium.com/response-to-climate-feedbacks-fact-check-of-mark-mills-wall-street-16b9742fe35a |last = Koonin| first = Steven | date= 2021-05-16| access-date=2023-03-13 |language=en}}</ref>

On August 21, 2023, an [https://www.hoover.org/research/hot-or-not-steven-koonin-questions-conventional-climate-science-and-methodology interview] with Koonin was released via the Stanford University Hoover Institution video series, Uncommon Knowledge with Peter Robinson.
